quarterly_data.quarter: Kurita Water Industries results briefing Q&A: Summary of the Q&A Session for 1Q of FY ending March 2027 (08-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management: inquiry levels in the Electronics Industry segment remained high on proactive customer investments; Kurita won orders not factored into its initial forecast, including multiple mid- and large-scale orders in China, South Korea, North America and Europe mainly from global accounts, and order progress is faster than expected against the 1H forecast. It expects to win large-scale orders in Japan and the US in 2Q, but did not raise its order forecast because Electronics orders can be highly variable and it wants to monitor 2Q first. Recurring contract-based services are running ahead of assumptions, mainly on high capacity utilization at existing customers' plants. An increasing proportion of facilities projects are waste water-related.

quarterly_data.quarter: Kurita Water Industries results briefing Q&A: Summary of the Q&A Session for 1Q of FY ending March 2027 (08-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management: order intake is rising at a rapid pace; current production capacity is sufficient for the orders won this fiscal year, but production capacity remains tight, and Kurita is transforming its production process, for example by automating design.

quarterly_data.quarter: Kurita Water Industries results briefing Q&A: Summary of the Q&A Session for 1Q of FY ending March 2027 (08-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management: the Electronics Industry additional costs relate to one specific project in North America, Kurita's first there; including specification changes they were around 2 billion yen, caused by rework on US-specific standards and by the customer replacing the design and construction company. A slight lingering impact is expected in 2Q, limited to 1H; other projects are proceeding in line with assumptions.

quarterly_data.quarter: Kurita Water Industries results briefing Q&A: Summary of the Q&A Session for 1Q of FY ending March 2027 (08-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management: the Middle East conflict had minimal impact on the General Industry segment in 1Q (direct demand impact and higher costs in EMEA); higher raw material, packaging and logistics costs in Japan were passed through to customers, so the cost-of-sales ratio barely deteriorated. Overall 1Q results were in line with assumptions and Kurita sees solid progress toward its full-year forecasts.
